It was set to true for four entries in commit 77947c1 without a source being read; those four were checked or reverted on 2026-09-19, and tests/test_legal_rules_verification.py now fails if a verified entry carries no verified_on, no verified_by, or a source_url that is only a domain. Entries verified on 2026-09-19 were read in the consolidated text in force that day on wetten.overheid.nl, with two exceptions recorded in their own verified_by: RS-TIED-HOUSING, which rests on a published advice rather than on law, and the 2026 health-insurance premium figure. Dutch rules for the temporary agency sector are changing: Waadi arts. 9a, 10 and 12 have amendments scheduled for 01-01-2027, art. 8 for 31-12-2026, the WTTA admission regime in chapter 3a enters into force on 01-01-2027 and the registration duty in art. 7a lapses on 01-01-2028, and BW 7:672 changes on 01-01-2028.
meta.how_to_verify: Open source_url, find the article, confirm the text still says what legal_basis claims, then set verified:true and verified_on to today's date. If the rule changed, update what_it_means too. The minimum wage figure changes every 1 January and 1 July. See Current status and limitations in README.md.

statutory_minimum_wage_hourly_eur.verified_by: Read WML art. 8(1) on wetten.overheid.nl on 2026-09-19 (geldend van 01-07-2026). The statute carries the un-indexed figure per hour with the editorial note 'per 1 juli 2026: EUR 14,99', which is the figure stored here; art. 8(1)(b) gives the corresponding monthly figure as EUR 2.337,00. Taken from the statute itself rather than from an information page about it. It changes every 1 January and 1 July. Documentary check against the published text, not legal advice; no team member has countersigned it.
statutory_minimum_wage_hourly_eur.note: Gross statutory hourly minimum wage for a worker aged 21 or over, in force from 1 July 2026 (it was EUR 14.71 from 1 January 2026). The Netherlands moved to a statutory hourly minimum wage on 1 January 2024, so there is one hourly figure rather than a monthly figure divided by sector hours. Lower statutory rates apply to workers aged 15-20 (EUR 11.99 at 20, down to EUR 4.50 at 15) and are NOT modelled here: the checks assume an adult worker, which is the group this tool is for. The figure is revised every 1 January and 1 July, so it goes stale twice a year.

housing_deduction_max_share_of_minimum_w.verified_by: Read BMLMV art. 2a on wetten.overheid.nl on 2026-09-19 (BWBR0008222, geldend van 01-01-2023). 2a(1)(a) caps rent, the cost of individually metered utilities and service charges together at 'ten hoogste 25%' of the minimum wage applying to the worker for that payment term, and 2a(1)(b) attaches the landlord condition: a toegelaten instelling under art. 19(1) Woningwet, or certification against the CAO housing-quality norm by an accredited body. 2a(2) makes the authorisation void outright for a worker posted under the WagwEU, and 2a(3) requires copies of the tenancy and of the documents showing the landlord qualifies. Documentary check against the published text, not legal advice; no team member has countersigned it.
housing_deduction_max_share_of_minimum_w.note: Confirmed: Besluit minimumloon en minimumvakantiebijslag article 2a(1)(a) — rent, metered utilities and service costs together may be paid out of the minimum wage up to at most 25% of the minimum wage for that payment period. The 25% is not the whole rule. Article 2a also requires a written authorisation from the worker (art. 13(2) Wet minimumloon en minimumvakantiebijslag), copies of the tenancy agreement and supporting documents handed to the employer, and a landlord that is either a housing corporation (toegelaten instelling, art. 19(1) Woningwet) or certified against the collective-agreement housing-quality norm by an accredited body. An authorisation is void outright where the worker is posted to the Netherlands under the WagwEU. An amendment to article 2a is scheduled for 1 January 2027.

health_insurance_deduction_rule.verified_by: Read BMLMV art. 2b on wetten.overheid.nl on 2026-09-19 (BWBR0008222, geldend van 01-01-2023). 2b(1) caps the payments at 'het bedrag van de geraamde gemiddelde nominale premie die een verzekerde voor een zorgverzekering betaalt, vermeerderd met 10 procent, gedeeld door het aantal betalingstermijnen voor het betrokken kalenderjaar', and 2b(2) has the Minister of VWS fix that estimated premium annually by 1 November for the following year. The 2026 estimate of EUR 1.908,00 a year comes from the Regeling geraamde gemiddelde nominale premie 2026 of 24 October 2025, made under art. 2b(2); EUR 1.908,00 plus 10% is EUR 2.098,80 a year and EUR 174,90 a month, which are the figures stored here. Honest limit on this one: the ceiling and its formula were read in the Besluit itself, but the 2026 premium figure was taken from a report of that ministerial regulation rather than from the regulation's own text in the Staatscourant. Documentary check against the published text, not legal advice; no team member has countersigned it.
health_insurance_deduction_rule.note: Confirmed: Besluit minimumloon en minimumvakantiebijslag article 2b — the premium for the worker's health insurance plus any policy covering the compulsory excess may be paid out of the minimum wage up to the estimated average nominal premium plus 10%, divided by the number of payment periods in the calendar year. The Minister of Health sets the estimated average nominal premium by 1 November for the following year; for 2026 it is EUR 1,908 a year, so the ceiling is EUR 2,098.80 a year (EUR 174.90 a month). Article 2b also requires a written authorisation and copies of the policies. No check reads this value yet — it is recorded so the figure is here when one does.

assumed_hours_per_week_when_none_stated.note: An assumption, not a legal figure, and one that cannot be 'verified' against a source: Dutch law sets no statutory full-time week. It is used for one thing only - putting a wage or a deduction stated per week or per month onto the same footing as an hourly figure when the documents guarantee no hours - and any finding that depends on it is reported with the assumption stated. It stays verified:false so --check-setup keeps saying so. It was flipped to true in commit 77947c1 with no source and restored on 2026-09-19. DECIDED on 2026-09-22 (36 against 40, see docs/decisions.md): neither. Since 1 January 2024 the WML sets the minimum wage per hour worked (art. 8(1)(a)), and BMLMV art. 2a(1)(a) caps the housing deduction at 25% of the minimum wage applying to the worker for that payment term - so the ceiling follows the hours actually worked, not a notional week. The 36-hour figure belongs to the derivation of the referentiemaandloon, a monthly reference amount, and is not a basis for what an individual worker is owed; adopting it here would have produced a ceiling 10% lower than the law allows for a 40-hour worker. The checks therefore compare per hour, and this value is only the fallback that lets a weekly or monthly amount be converted at all. 40 is kept because it is the common full-time week in the sectors this tool is for; where it is used, the finding also states the ceiling per hour worked, which does not depend on it.

rules.title: You are being charged a fee for getting the job
rules.legal_basis: Wet allocatie arbeidskrachten door intermediairs (Waadi), article 9 - 'voor de terbeschikkingstelling wordt geen tegenprestatie bedongen van de arbeidskracht': no consideration may be demanded from the worker in return for being placed.
rules.what_it_means: An agency is not allowed to make you pay for being placed in work. A charge like this is void, which means you were never legally required to pay it — including if it has already been taken from your wage.
rules.user_action_hint: Ask, in writing, what this charge is for and which rule allows it.
rules.verified_by: Read the consolidated Waadi text on wetten.overheid.nl on 2026-09-19 (geldend van 01-07-2026 t/m heden). Artikel 9 in full: 'Bij het ter beschikking stellen van arbeidskrachten wordt voor de terbeschikkingstelling geen tegenprestatie bedongen van de arbeidskracht, die ter beschikking wordt gesteld.' That is the whole article, and it says what legal_basis claims it says. Documentary check against the published text, not legal advice; no team member has countersigned it.

rules.title: A clause stops you taking a job directly with the company you work at
rules.legal_basis: Waadi article 9a - the supplier may not obstruct an employment contract forming between the worker and the hirer after the placement ends, and article 9a(2) makes any clause to the contrary void. The single exception is a reasonable fee owed by the *hirer* to the agency for its services; it does not permit a charge to the worker.
rules.what_it_means: You are allowed to be hired directly by the company you are placed at. A clause that forbids this, or that makes you pay a penalty for it, has no legal force — even though it is written in your contract.
rules.user_action_hint: Keep a copy of this clause. It is useful evidence if you are later told you cannot move.
rules.verified_by: Read Waadi art. 9a on wetten.overheid.nl on 2026-09-19 (geldend van 01-07-2026). 9a(1) forbids the supplier placing obstacles in the way of an employment contract forming between the worker and the hirer after the placement ends. 9a(2): 'Elk beding in strijd met het eerste lid is nietig, met uitzondering van een beding op grond waarvan door degene aan wie de arbeidskracht ter beschikking is gesteld een redelijke vergoeding verschuldigd is aan degene die de arbeidskracht ter beschikking heeft gesteld' - the fee is owed by the hirer to the agency, never by the worker, which is the distinction this rule turns on. The page records a further amendment to art. 9a with effect from 01-01-2027. Documentary check against the published text, not legal advice; no team member has countersigned it.

rules.title: Your passport or ID is to be held by someone else
rules.legal_basis: Waadi article 7c. The worker hands over an identity document so that the agency can establish identity before the placement (7c(1) and (2)); the agency takes a copy into its administration (7c(3)); and it must destroy that copy as soon as it is no longer necessary for establishing identity, and at the latest four weeks after it was filed, unless the wage-tax duty in article 28(1)(f) of the Wet op de loonbelasting 1964 applies (7c(4)). The article provides for a copy that must be destroyed, and for nobody keeping the document itself. The Nederlandse Arbeidsinspectie lists being unable to dispose of one's own ID or passport among the signals of labour exploitation.
rules.what_it_means: Your identity document is yours. Nobody you work for or rent from is entitled to keep it. Being unable to get your passport back is one of the clearest warning signs of exploitation.
rules.user_action_hint: This is one to raise with a confidential advice organisation rather than with your employer first.
rules.verified_by: Pinned to an article on 2026-09-19, as the pre-submission verification review asked for. Read Waadi art. 7c on wetten.overheid.nl (geldend van 01-07-2026): 7c(3) 'neemt een afschrift van het document, bedoeld in het eerste lid, op in diens administratie'; 7c(4) 'vernietigt het afschrift, bedoeld in het derde lid, zodra dit afschrift niet meer noodzakelijk is voor de vaststelling, bedoeld in het tweede lid, maar uiterlijk vier weken nadat het afschrift in de administratie is opgenomen.' Read the Nederlandse Arbeidsinspectie page on recognising and reporting labour exploitation (https://www.nlarbeidsinspectie.nl/onderwerpen/herkennen-en-melden-arbeidsuitbuiting) the same day; its list of signals includes 'niet kunnen beschikken over hun ID/eigen paspoort'. The earlier basis - the Wet op de identificatieplicht, the copying duty under the Wet arbeid vreemdelingen and the AVG taken together - has been replaced by the single article that governs this situation for agency work. Documentary check against the published text, not legal advice; no team member has countersigned it.

rules.title: More is being taken from your wage than the law allows
rules.legal_basis: Wet minimumloon en minimumvakantiebijslag article 13(1) - the minimum wage is not open to deduction or set-off by the employer. Article 13(2) allows an exception only for payment obligations designated by order in council and only under a written authorisation from the worker; those obligations, and their ceilings, are set out in articles 2a and 2b of the Besluit minimumloon en minimumvakantiebijslag (housing at most 25% of the minimum wage; health insurance at most the estimated average nominal premium plus 10%).
rules.what_it_means: Your employer may only take certain things out of the part of your wage that equals the minimum wage, and only up to a limit. What these documents set out goes past that limit.
rules.user_action_hint: Keep every payslip. The amounts actually deducted are what matters, not only what the contract says.
rules.verified_by: Read WML art. 13 on wetten.overheid.nl on 2026-09-19 (geldend van 01-07-2026) and the Besluit minimumloon en minimumvakantiebijslag arts. 2a and 2b the same day (BWBR0008222, geldend van 01-01-2023). 13(1): 'Het minimumloon is niet vatbaar voor inhouding of verrekening door de werkgever'. 13(2) allows inhouding only for payment obligations designated by order in council and only under a written volmacht. BMLMV art. 2a(1)(a) caps rent, individually metered utility costs and service charges together at 25% of the minimum wage for that payment term; 2a(1)(b) requires the landlord to be a toegelaten instelling under art. 19(1) Woningwet or certified against the CAO housing norm; 2a(2) makes the volmacht void for a worker posted under the WagwEU; 2a(3) requires the worker to hand over copies of the tenancy. Art. 2b(1) caps health-insurance payments at the estimated average nominal premium plus 10%, divided by the number of payment terms. Documentary check against the published text, not legal advice; no team member has countersigned it.

rules.title: What you are left with is below the minimum wage
rules.legal_basis: Wet minimumloon en minimumvakantiebijslag - since 1 January 2024 the statutory minimum applies per hour worked, so what is left after lawful deductions must still reach the hourly minimum for every hour. Article 13a(1) also requires hours worked beyond the agreed working time to be paid no later than the following pay period.
rules.what_it_means: Once the deductions in these documents are subtracted, the amount left for each hour you work is below the legal minimum.
rules.user_action_hint: Write down your actual hours each week, including waiting time and travel between sites if you are told to do it.
rules.verified_by: Read WML arts. 8 and 13a on wetten.overheid.nl on 2026-09-19 (geldend van 01-07-2026). Art. 8(1)(a) states the minimum wage 'per uur', carrying the editorial note 'per 1 juli 2026: EUR 14,99' - which confirms both the hourly structure introduced on 1 January 2024 and the figure the computed checks use. Art. 13a(1) requires working time beyond the agreed working time to be paid no later than the pay period following the one in which it arose. Note for whoever revisits the arithmetic: art. 8(1)(c) reckons proportionally with a 36-hour week for the purposes of arts. 7, 7a, 11, 13, 13a, 15 and 16. Documentary check against the published text, not legal advice; no team member has countersigned it.

rules.title: Losing the job also means losing your home
rules.legal_basis: Not unlawful in itself. Recommendation 4.4.B of the second advice of the Aanjaagteam Bescherming Arbeidsmigranten (Roemer commission), 'Geen tweederangsburgers', 30 October 2020, is headed 'Ontkoppeling huur- en arbeidscontract op papier en in de praktijk': an integrated contract for work and housing may be offered as a service, but it also makes the worker dependent on the employer, and the Aanjaagteam therefore advises working towards decoupling employment contracts from rental contracts. Recommendation 4.4.A asks for an independent tenancy for every form of accommodation.
rules.what_it_means: Your accommodation is provided through your work, and your work can end at short notice. A Dutch colleague who loses this job loses income. You would lose income and your home on the same day.
rules.user_action_hint: Ask in writing whether you can stay in the accommodation, and for how long, if the work ends.
rules.verified_by: URL replaced and the recommendation pinned on 2026-09-19, as the pre-submission verification review asked for. The previous link (rijksoverheid.nl/documenten/rapporten/2020/10/30/tweede-advies-aanjaagteam-bescherming-arbeidsmigranten) is the one-page Kamerbrief; the advice itself is its attachment, and source_url now points at that report on open.overheid.nl. Read it the same day: 69 pages, 'Geen tweederangsburgers. Aanbevelingen om misstanden bij arbeidsmigranten in Nederland tegen te gaan', Aanjaagteam Bescherming Arbeidsmigranten, 30 oktober 2020. Recommendation 4.4.B, chapter 4, report page 44: 'Waar een integraal contract voor arbeid en wonen als service richting de arbeidsmigrant kan worden gezien, wordt de arbeidsmigrant hierdoor ook afhankelijk van de werkgever. Daarom adviseert het Aanjaagteam te streven naar ontkoppeling van arbeidscontracten en huurcontracten.' A recommendation is not law and this rule does not present it as one; what is verified is that the recommendation exists and says this. Documentary check against the published text, not legal advice; no team member has countersigned it.

rules.title: Your home, transport and insurance all depend on this one job
rules.legal_basis: Not unlawful. Reported because the combination concentrates every risk on the worker.
rules.what_it_means: More than one essential thing in your life is supplied by the same company that employs you. If the work stops, several of them stop together, which makes it much harder to stay and look for other work.
rules.user_action_hint: Ask which of these you can keep, and on what terms, if you change employer.
rules.verified_by: Nothing to verify against a source: this rule reports a combination as a risk and asserts no legal basis.

rules.title: No guaranteed hours, but you may not work elsewhere
rules.legal_basis: Not unlawful in itself, though the combination may be challengeable. Reported as risk.
rules.what_it_means: You are not promised any minimum amount of work, but you are also not allowed to take other work. In a week with few shifts you have no way to make up the income.
rules.user_action_hint: Ask in writing how many hours per week you are guaranteed, and what happens in a week with no work.
rules.verified_by: Nothing to verify against a source: this rule reports a combination as a risk and asserts no legal basis.

rules.title: You start in debt, and leaving early costs you money
rules.legal_basis: Not unlawful in itself. The combination of a repayable advance with a penalty for early departure is a recognised indicator of debt-driven dependency.
rules.what_it_means: Money spent getting you here is being repaid out of your wage, and leaving before a certain point would cost you extra. Together these make it expensive to leave a job that turns out to be different from what you were told.
rules.user_action_hint: Ask for the total amount you owe and the exact date it is repaid by.
rules.verified_by: Nothing to verify against a source: this rule reports a combination as a risk and asserts no legal basis.

rules.title: The notice period binds you but not your employer
rules.legal_basis: Burgerlijk Wetboek article 7:672(4) sets the worker's notice period at one month. Article 7:672(8) allows that to be extended in writing to at most six months, but then requires the employer's notice period to be at least double the worker's. A contract that gives the worker a longer notice period than the employer is therefore contrary to 7:672(8), not merely unbalanced; only a collective agreement may shorten the employer's side, and never below the worker's (7:672(9)). Reported as a risk rather than an illegality because which period actually applies depends on the collective agreement and on the length of service.
rules.what_it_means: You must give more warning before leaving than your employer must give before ending your work. That means you can be let go faster than you can leave. Dutch law generally requires the opposite: if your notice period is extended, your employer's has to be at least twice as long as yours.
rules.user_action_hint: Ask what notice each side must give, and get the answer in writing.
rules.verified_by: Read BW art. 7:672 on wetten.overheid.nl on 2026-09-19 (Boek 7, geldend van 01-07-2026). 672(4): 'De door de werknemer in acht te nemen termijn van opzegging bedraagt een maand.' 672(8): that period may be departed from in writing, on extension the worker's may not exceed six months and the employer's may be 'niet korter dan het dubbele van die voor de werknemer'. 672(9): a collective agreement may shorten the employer's period, but never below the worker's. The page records an amendment to art. 672 with effect from 01-01-2028. Documentary check against the published text, not legal advice; no team member has countersigned it.

rules.title: There are penalties you could be charged
rules.legal_basis: Burgerlijk Wetboek article 7:650 - a penalty clause must be in writing, must name the exact rule broken and the exact amount, and must state where the money goes, which may not be the employer's own benefit. For a worker earning at or below the minimum wage these requirements cannot be contracted out of, the combined penalties in any one week may not exceed half a day's wage, and article 7:650(6) makes any clause in breach void.
rules.what_it_means: These documents set out amounts you could be charged in certain situations. If you earn the minimum wage, the law caps all penalties in one week at half a day's pay and voids a clause that goes further. Whether a particular charge would hold up is a separate question, but it can be taken from your pay first and disputed afterwards.
rules.user_action_hint: Ask for a list of every situation in which money can be charged to you.
rules.verified_by: Read BW art. 7:650 on wetten.overheid.nl on 2026-09-19 (Boek 7, geldend van 01-07-2026). 650(1) requires the contract to name the rules whose breach is penalised and the amount; 650(2) requires writing; 650(3) requires the destination of the money to be stated precisely and forbids it benefiting the employer directly or indirectly; 650(4) requires a fixed amount; 650(5) caps combined penalties in any one week at half a day's wage and forbids any single penalty above that. 650(6) makes every clause in breach void and permits derogation from leden 3, 4 and 5 only in writing and only for workers whose hourly wage exceeds the minimum wage - so at or below the minimum wage these cannot be contracted out of, which is what this rule claims. Documentary check against the published text, not legal advice; no team member has countersigned it.

rules.title: You are signing an open-ended permission to deduct from your wage
rules.legal_basis: Wet minimumloon en minimumvakantiebijslag article 13(2) permits payment out of the minimum wage only under a written authorisation, and only for the obligations designated in articles 2a and 2b of the Besluit minimumloon en minimumvakantiebijslag. Both require the worker to hand over copies of the underlying tenancy or insurance policy, and both cap the amount, so an authorisation naming no amount, no end date and no specific obligation cannot satisfy them.
rules.what_it_means: The authorisation you are being asked to sign does not name a fixed amount or an end date. It allows money to be taken from your wage in situations you have not seen yet.
rules.user_action_hint: Ask for the authorisation to name the exact amounts and the date it ends.
rules.verified_by: Read the Besluit minimumloon en minimumvakantiebijslag arts. 2a and 2b on wetten.overheid.nl on 2026-09-19 (BWBR0008222, geldend van 01-01-2023). Both provisions are built the same way: a written volmacht for one named obligation, copies of the underlying document handed to the employer (2a(3) the tenancy and the proof that the landlord qualifies; 2b(3) the zorgpolis), and a ceiling (2a(1)(a) 25% of the minimum wage for that payment term; 2b(1) the estimated average nominal premium plus 10%, divided by the number of payment terms). An authorisation that names no amount, no end date and no specific obligation cannot satisfy either of them. Documentary check against the published text, not legal advice; no team member has countersigned it.

rules.title: You may be entitled to the same pay as the company's own staff
rules.legal_basis: Waadi article 8(1) - a worker placed other than by payrolling is entitled to at least the same terms of employment as staff in the same or equivalent roles at the hiring company, covering pay and other allowances, and working time, rest, night work, breaks, holiday length and public holidays. Article 8(2) falls back to the sector where the hirer employs nobody comparable. Article 8(4) allows a collective agreement to derogate, which is why this is reported as a question to ask rather than as a breach. An amendment is scheduled for 31 December 2026.
rules.what_it_means: Dutch law says agency workers should get the same pay and conditions as the hiring company's own staff doing the same work, unless a collective agreement sets something different. Most people never find out which applies to them. You are entitled to ask which company you are placed at, what its staff are paid for your job, and which collective agreement is being used.
rules.user_action_hint: Ask, in writing, which company you will be working at and which collective agreement applies to your job there.
rules.verified_by: Read Waadi art. 8 on wetten.overheid.nl on 2026-09-19 (geldend van 01-07-2026). 8(1) gives a worker placed other than by payrolling the right to at least the same terms as employees in the same or equivalent roles at the hiring company: (a) pay and other allowances, (b) working time including overtime, rest, night work, breaks, holiday length and public holidays under arrangements in force at that company. 8(2) falls back to the sector where the hirer employs nobody comparable. 8(4): 'Bij collectieve arbeidsovereenkomst kan worden afgeweken van het eerste tot en met het derde lid' - which is exactly why this rule is phrased as a question to ask and not as a breach to assert. The page records a scheduled amendment to art. 8 with effect from 31-12-2026. Documentary check against the published text, not legal advice; no team member has countersigned it.

rules.title: Part of your pay is labelled as expenses rather than wage
rules.legal_basis: Wet minimumloon en minimumvakantiebijslag article 6(1)(e): allowances, in so far as they can be regarded as meeting necessary costs the worker incurs in connection with the employment - which expressly include the costs of travel, accommodation and food - are not 'loon' for the purposes of that Act. Pay relabelled as an expense allowance therefore does not count towards the statutory minimum wage, and because article 15(1) sets holiday allowance at at least 8% of loon, it lowers that too. Article 6(4) adds that where a worker temporarily works in a country other than the one where they usually work, and the terms of employment do not specify which parts of an allowance meet necessary costs, the whole allowance is treated as such an allowance.
rules.what_it_means: Part of what you are paid is recorded as a reimbursement of costs rather than as wage. Money labelled that way does not count towards the minimum wage you are owed, and your holiday allowance is calculated as a percentage of wage without it. Your take-home pay can look the same while the amount the law protects is lower.
rules.user_action_hint: Ask what your gross wage is before any expense allowances, and check that figure on your payslip.
rules.verified_by: Pinned to an article on 2026-09-19, as the pre-submission verification review asked for; the previous source_url was the Belastingdienst home page. Read WML arts. 6 and 15 on wetten.overheid.nl (geldend van 01-07-2026). Art. 6(1)(e) excludes from loon 'vergoedingen voor zover zij geacht kunnen worden te strekken tot bestrijding van noodzakelijke kosten, die de werknemer in verband met zijn dienstbetrekking heeft te maken, waaronder in ieder geval worden begrepen kosten voor reizen, huisvesting of voeding'; art. 15(1) sets vakantiebijslag at 'ten minste ... 8% van zijn ten laste van de werkgever komende loon'. The rule's earlier claim - that this lowers the basis for pension, sick pay and unemployment benefit - has been narrowed to what this check actually establishes. That wider claim runs through the definition of loon in the Wet financiering sociale verzekeringen, which has not been read, so it is no longer asserted in what_it_means. Documentary check against the published text, not legal advice; no team member has countersigned it.
